---
title: "Q2: Divergent reasoning"
description: "How alternative reasoning strategies can emerge from the same starting model."
---

[**Component:** Navigator - finds the points where the reasoning could have gone another way, and checks whether the different routes are genuinely different approaches.]{.text-blue}

::: {.research-question}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Q2: Why do identical agents develop different reasoning strategies?**

This note investigates whether branching at high-entropy decision points can create genuinely different reasoning strategies, rather than only different phrasings or final outcomes.
:::

**Procedure.**

1. One agent produces a complete reasoning trace and a final answer. This is the reference
   trace.
2. The token-level entropy of the reference trace is recorded, and the highest-entropy
   positions are identified as candidate decision points.
3. At each decision point, generation is resumed from the preceding prefix with a different
   continuation, and each branch is run to completion.
4. The outcomes of the branches are compared against the outcome of the reference trace.
   A decision point is important if resampling it changes the distribution over final
   answers. **This is its counterfactual point**
5. Where the reference trace failed and its branches succeed, the decision point marks
   where the reasoning went wrong. That position, and the continuation that recovered from
   it, can be recorded for reuse.

**Working assumptions for this mechanism.**

- High-entropy positions correspond to meaningful choices in the reasoning rather than to
  surface variation in wording.
- Failure in a reasoning trace can be localised to a small number of positions rather than
  being distributed across the whole trace.
- The alternative continuations produced at a decision point represent different strategies,
  not different phrasings of the same strategy.

**Open questions for this mechanism.**

- Do branches taken at the same decision point differ in strategy, or only in outcome?
- What distinguishes a decision point that produces a useful alternative from one that
  produces an equivalent restatement?
- How should a recorded failure point be abstracted so that it transfers to a different
  problem, rather than being tied to the trace it came from?
- Which level is the right unit of branching: the token, the sentence, or the reasoning step?

**Scope note.** This mechanism addresses only the first source of divergence listed above,
stochasticity. It says nothing about divergence arising from experience, memory, or
communication. It also operates on the model's output distribution rather than its internal
representations; the internal version of the same question is Q3.

**Supporting literature and concepts.** Token entropy and forking tokens; entropy-guided
decoding and branching; counterfactual importance and step-level attribution; tree search
over reasoning traces.

**Related papers.**

- [Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01939) establishes that a small minority of tokens carry most of the branching behaviour in a chain of thought, and that these tokens act as forks steering the model toward different reasoning pathways.
- [Thought Anchors: Which LLM Reasoning Steps Matter?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.19143) measures the counterfactual importance of each sentence in a reasoning trace by resampling from that position, .and finds that planning and uncertainty-management steps matter more than computation steps.
- [ETTRL: Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in LLM Test-Time Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11356) implements fork-based exploration at high-entropy tokens and reuses the low-entropy segments between forks.
- [Improving Multi-Agent Debate with Sparse Communication Topology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11776) tests how changing agent communication structures affects collective reasoning.

**Possible investigation:** Take one open-weights reasoning model and a set of problems with
checkable answers. Generate a reference trace per problem, record token entropy, branch at
the highest-entropy positions, and run each branch to a final answer. Then cluster the
branches by strategy rather than by correctness, and ask whether branching at a decision
point produces genuinely distinct approaches or only distinct wordings of one approach.

```text
                 Reference trace
                        |
        low entropy ----+---- low entropy
                        |
                 decision point
            ------------+------------
            |           |           |
        branch A    branch B    branch C
            |           |           |
            v           v           v
         outcome     outcome     outcome
            |           |           |
            ------------+------------
                        v
          Counterfactual importance of
              this decision point
                        v
           Strategy comparison across
                     branches
```

**Why this matters for the rest of the work.** This experiment does not answer a question
on its own. If I want a group of agents that each do
something different, I first need a way to tell whether two agents are actually doing
different things, or just saying the same thing in different words. There is no agreed way
to do that for reasoning yet. Working out how to group reasoning traces by approach is that
tool. Once I have it, I can give each branch its own memory and follow it across many
problems (Q2), keep a store of different approaches rather than only the best-scoring one,
and pass approaches between agents to see if they transfer (Q4).



**Status:** <span class="research-status is-exploring">Exploring</span>
